scope: Curiosity V3 free-exploration real-model performance smoke

limitChange.rationale: The 120-second target was a product goal, not a technical constraint: generation already runs in the out-of-band curiosity-worker, so no request timeout enforced it. Rather than change the five-stage serial topology or keep searching OpenRouter for a faster strict-structured-output model, the owner chose to relax the total-duration goal to 10 minutes.
limitChange.perCallTimeout: CURIOSITY_MODEL_TIMEOUT_MS was raised from 120000 to 300000 ms in the same decision — the maximum the validator in lib/curiosity/server-model.ts accepts. A single stage may now run up to 5 minutes; two such stages would still leave the 600000 ms total gate satisfiable. The in-code default for environments that do not set the variable is unchanged at 120000.

question: 飞机为什么能飞起来？

attempts.note: Before per-stage instrumentation; exceeded the hard limit.
1536-token knowledge budget produced no structured output.
OpenRouter reported no endpoint supporting the required strict structured-output parameters.
Question modeling alone consumed 91.9 seconds, so the five-stage serial route cannot meet the 120-second hard limit.
The initial pass was fast, but the quality agent rejected both the original and the allowed redesign for age-appropriateness, grounding and narration coverage.
The second DeepSeek sample exceeded the hard limit before the GLM quality review began, so the route has unacceptable latency variance.
The first quality review rejected and correctly triggered the allowed scene/presentation/quality retry. The hard limit was already exceeded before that retry.

reevaluationAgainstNewLimit.note: The attempts above are unchanged raw measurements taken under the 120000 ms limit; their individual notes still argue against that old limit. Nothing below has been re-measured — this is a re-reading of existing samples against 600000 ms.
reevaluationAgainstNewLimit.glm-5.2: Both samples now fit: 139200 ms end-to-end, and 190581 ms before an allowed quality retry that would add roughly the observed scene+presentation+quality cost. GLM-5.2 produced valid strict-schema output at every stage in every sample, so the limit was its only blocker. It is the leading candidate.
reevaluationAgainstNewLimit.deepseek-v4-flash: Latency is no longer disqualifying, but the QUALITY_REJECTED sample is a quality failure independent of the limit and remains unresolved.
reevaluationAgainstNewLimit.kimi-k2.5: Only the question stage was ever measured (91901 ms); no full five-stage sample exists, so it stays unverified.
reevaluationAgainstNewLimit.qwen-flash / glm-5.1: Still disqualified for lack of real strict structured-output support; unaffected by the limit change.

conclusion: The 120-second release gate was retired by product decision on 2026-08-17 in favour of a 600-second gate, so the failure recorded in this file no longer stands. No run has yet been measured under the new limit. The next step is the 60-run final gate on the openrouter:z-ai/glm-5.2 route; a pass there, not this re-reading, is what unblocks release.
